claims.text: The Spui is a famous square in the centre of Amsterdam, but for centuries it was actually a body of water forming the city's southern border.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The name roughly translates to a 'lockable water discharge', referring to its original function before the area was transformed.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The water was eventually completely filled in back in 1882 to create the wide open square that you see today.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Following a major renovation in 1996, the bustling square was made largely car-free to create a much safer and pedestrian-friendly environment.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The area is well known for hosting an incredibly popular weekly book market every single Friday.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: It also completely transforms again on Sundays to host a lovely outdoor market entirely dedicated to unique art and antiques.
claims.subject: self
